Maya Lin: Heads-up — Halcyon chat traffic jumped after they enabled the "live-assistant" pipeline. Token spend doubled in 36h. Need a concise QBR-ready note and an immediate mitigation plan. cc @Ethan
Ethan Cole: Looking now. 36h burn = $13.4k, projected 30d at current = $268k. Their normal run-rate ~= $55k/mo. Credits remaining = $40k, retainer = $25k/mo, retainer expires in 13 days. :grimacing:
Priya Nair: Any idea what exploded tokens? Is it user context growth, assistant verbosity, or function outputs?
Ethan Cole: Quick breakdown by token source: user context (convo history) = 42%, assistant responses = 38%, tool/function outputs (structured JSON) = 12%, system prompts & metadata = 8%. Biggest driver is unbounded convo history + long assistant responses with verbose citations.
Maya Lin: Customer asked for full transcript context for audit compliance which is inflating token windows. They also enabled tool-calling that dumps large JSON blobs. We should propose QBR mitigations: prompt compression, context pruning, response-length caps, and tool-output truncation.
Priya Nair: For the QBR slide suggest 3 quick knobs: (A) enable context-summarization (compress older turns to a 1-2 sentence summary every N messages), (B) enforce assistant max_tokens=256 + streaming end signals, (C) truncate or hash tool outputs (store full payload in S3 and reference key).
Ethan Cole: Scenario forecasts if applied: status_quo = $268k, prompt-compress + response-cap = $140k, plus tool-output-hash = $96k. Notes: compression may slightly degrade traceability; we can offer a 30-day archived full transcript on request as a compromise.
finance-bot: Account HALCYON: credits_remaining = $40,000, monthly_retainer = $25,000, retainer_expiry = 2026-04-05, auto_renew = false.
quota-bot: ALERT: HALCYON hit 72% of credits at 1769998820. Billing owner notified.
Maya Lin: Draft mitigation snippet for QBR (policy-style): ```yaml
policy: chat_token_guard
soft_threshold_usd: 20000
hard_threshold_usd: 32000
soft_action: notify-cs + recommend-compression
hard_action: enforce-response-cap + swap-tool-output-to-reference
```
Priya Nair: Ops playbook (two-line) for engineers we can include in appendix: ```bash
# enable conversation compression for account
rwctl accounts set --account HALCYON --feature convo_summarization --window 10 --summary_len 2
# enforce assistant response cap and tool-output hashing
rwctl accounts set-route --account HALCYON --route assistant --max_tokens 256 --tool_output_mode reference
```
Ethan Cole: With those toggles the projected 30d spend drops to ~$96k. If customer wants stricter guarantees we can add a per-account hard throttle that returns 429 on excess token rate.
Maya Lin: Action items: Ethan — paste the three scenario numbers and a tiny sparkline into the QBR slide. Priya — write a 2-line customer-facing note framing this as "predictability + audit-safe archive option" and prepare the enablement invite (30m). I'll coordinate AE for a short staged commit ask.
Ethan Cole: Will upload numbers and sparkline by EOD.
Priya Nair: Draft customer blurb: "We noticed a recent rise in token usage tied to longer conversation history and verbose tool outputs. We can reduce monthly spend by ~60% with nondisruptive measures (context compression, response caps, tool-output references). Weoffer a 30-minute technical workshop and an optional 30-day archived transcript service for audits"
Maya Lin: Perfect. Meeting 15:00 to finalize slides and the renewal recommendation. :thumbsup:
Ethan Cole: See you 15:00. Priya — bring the sample invite.
quota-bot: Reminder scheduled: QBR prep meeting for HALCYON on 2026-03-26T15:00:00Z.
